questions.ask: What is your date of birth?
What is the postcode of the address we have for you?

intents.hardship: Financial hardship: job loss, illness, cannot cover essentials.
intents.dispute: "This isn't my debt" or "I never had that product".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower instalments.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.opening: Hello, this is Isla, a digital assistant calling from Glenmorrow Savings Bank. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I'm Isla, a digital assistant calling from Glenmorrow Savings Bank.
lines.scam: I understand your caution. I will never ask for your PIN or passwords, and you can call us back on the number on our official website.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I've confirmed I'm speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details about this call.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. It will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {title} {last_name}?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, we can only call back between 9 am and 6:30 pm, today or on the next two business days. Is there another time that would suit?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss the reason for my call with {title} {last_name}.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We'll call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry for the trouble, and thank you for letting me know.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_why: We ask these questions to protect your personal information.
lines.id_explain: I can only discuss this call with the right person, so I need to confirm who I'm speaking with.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't go on with this call.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match the details we hold.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't go on with this call. Please visit a branch or log in to online banking.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you, {first_name}. I'm calling about overdue payments with Glenmorrow Savings Bank.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} in arrears and is {days} days overdue.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay both in full today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. The lowest amount I can accept is {amount}. Could you pay that on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't accept an amount below {floor}.
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, that is still below what I can accept.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed. Could you choose today or a later date?
lines.not_business_day: That day isn't a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work for you?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can accept is {date}. Could you pay by then?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day could you pay?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: To repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read back what we agreed.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can accept is {deadline}, so I've used that date.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, the promise for your {name} could not be recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take two business days to show, so I won't ask for a promise on this one.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask for a payment promise on this one.
lines.hardship: I'm sorry to hear you're going through this. I'm passing you to our care team, who can help.
lines.hardship_declined: I understand. Let's leave it there for today.
lines.hardship_short: Shall I put you through now?
lines.restructure_line: I'll pass you to our arrears solutions team, who can talk to you about payment plans.
lines.human_ask_help: I can help with most things on this call. Can I help you with it myself?
lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change a promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book that callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer didn't go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system isn't responding right now.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.
lines.no_band_line: I'm sorry, I can't discuss your {name} on this call.

assumptions: The memo (19 Oct 2026, effective 2 Nov 2026) overrides policy v3.2 and the old code list where they differ, as both the email and the memo say.
Bands follow memo A: early is 1-14 days, mid is 15-30, late is 31-60. Deadlines and attempts (1/2/3) are unchanged.
Holidays: 30 Nov 2026, 25 Dec 2026, 28 Dec 2026, 1 Jan 2027 and 4 Jan 2027 come from rule 11. Memo B adds 11 Dec 2026. 24 Dec 2026 is a business day.
Memo C retires the reason code 'refused'. 'declined' is used for both the close_call reason (no_ptp/declined) and the add_note reason, which also matches the API enums.

The callback window is 09:00-18:30 inclusive (memo D replaces 09:00-20:00). Allowed days are today or the next two business days, and the time must be later than now. business_days_only is true because calls are only placed on business days and memo B forbids callbacks on 11 Dec.
Callback max_asks is 2: after the first time outside the window the agent asks once more, then closes as no_contact/no_callback.

Identity: date of birth first, then postcode. The date of birth is sent as DDMMYYYY (strftime %d%m%Y). The postcode is sent in capitals with one space before the last 3 characters. Postcodes get no fixed length because UK postcodes vary in length.
Two wrong answers in total end the check (rule 9; the memo confirms this limit stands). A numeric date is read day first (dmy), because the bank is in the UK and the system uses DDMMYYYY.

The verify_identity response has no hint field (its fields are ok, error, verified, wrong_answers_left, all_verified), so response.hint is empty and hints is empty. Unreadable answers come back as ok=false and are not counted, so reject_values is empty.

The floor is 30% of arrears_amount, rounded up to the next whole pound. An amount that is already whole stays as it is. The memo confirms the 25% idea was rejected. monthly_payment is never used. If the rounded floor were ever above the arrears amount, the floor is capped at the full arrears amount.
get_account amounts are in pounds (amount_scale 1). create_promise takes pence (promise_scale 100).
The mid-band deadline is today plus 14 calendar days. If that is not a business day, it moves to the business day before (rule 14). previous_business_day is used as the general adjustment.
The late-band deadline is the last business day of the current month. If today is already that day, the last business day of the next month is used (roll_if_not_after_today).

Ladder: step 1 is the full amount today (rules 16 and 20). Step 2 is the full amount on the 5th business day after today, or on the deadline if that is earlier, so the engine caps this date at the product's deadline. Step 3 is the floor on the deadline. Under rule 21, if the customer said the full amount is too much, step 2 offers the floor on step 2's date (full_or_floor).

The opening ask (full amount today) counts as attempt 1 (rule 20). With two products, a flat no to 'both in full today' counts as step 1 for each product (rule 23). Early-band products therefore get no further proposals after the opening ask.
too_much_floor keeps the default 'attempt_1'. The brief says the floor is offered on the next step's date, and the opening ask already used attempt 1.

A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline. If the customer names a non-business day, the agent offers the next business day, or the deadline if the next business day is after it.

Hardship: the brief transfers straight to care_team and closes as handoff/care with no note, so the hardship event uses handoff/care and note ''. hardship_short and hardship_declined are fallback lines only.
No notes are written on any transfer (rule 29). Promises already recorded stay.
notes.enabled is true: every product that ends without a promise gets one add_note (rule 25).
A paid claim or a dispute on one product does not end the call (rule 25).
Texting a payment link was dropped (see the email), so sms_line is empty.
If create_promise fails twice for a product, the agent says the record_failed line and notes system_error (rule 30).
The brief does not define 'next <weekday>', so the default following_week is used.
The brief does not cover changing a recorded promise, so promise_change says it cannot be changed on this call.
The brief calls the floor 'the floor'. The customer hears 'minimum amount' instead.
max_not_talk (2), purpose_is_decline (true), after_promise.ask_anything_else (true) and human.ask_first (true, per rule 29) use the defaults or the brief's rules.
The brief does not cover days in arrears outside 1-60 (calls only target 1-60), so bands_outside is null.
Closing codes follow rule 31: ptp and claims_paid are sent without a reason; no_ptp uses the note reason of the first product, in get_account order, that was not noted paid.
